loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

# Readings — kernel-defs (spec v0 §21–§75, §79–§81)

Modules: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/{Basic,Ops,Invariants}.lean`.
Machine-checked witnesses quoted below: `scratchpad/kd/Readings.lean` (W1–W4) and the `Examples`
section of `Invariants.lean` (E-63.8). Full path of the scratch file:
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/kd/Readings.lean`
(checked with `lake env lean`, no error).

Each entry: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes.
"[policy]" marks a reading fixed by `policy.md` (recorded as required); the others are mine.

## A. Spec problems (need arbitration)

**SP-A1 [blocking for §57, transfer] §63 admits an ownership cycle.** Policy removes the draft clause
`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`. W1 (decide): statics `src`(0, Init), `prov`(1, Init);
`alloc(prov, owner src)` → place 2 owned by 0; `alloc(prov, owner 2)` → place 3 owned by 2;
`TransferPre K0 c2 0 3` holds (all fields, §63.8 included). After the step places 2 and 3 own each
other: root 2 is active, held by unusable place 3 (§49.8 false) and covers leaf 2 of unusable place 2
(`NoDangling` false). §58 ("must ... preserve the relevant invariants") vs §63's clause list. The next
wave's `transfer_preserves` is false as stated for these definitions.

**SP-A2 §71.2 vs §36 [policy: record].** §71.2 "permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid
`writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata"; §36 "Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant
the right to create ... exclusive authority over the administered storage". `AllocStatic.providerRight`
follows §71.2 literally: `alloc` can create a root `Modify` authority with only an `Observe` right on a
`SharedMutable` provider. Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, an `Observe` derivative held by the
frame and no `Modify` on it: §71.2 accepts, §36 forbids.

**SP-A3 §69.2/§70.3: descendants of authorities released by the effect [policy for §69; by analogy
for §70].** W2 (decide): `x`, `r` leaves; `a := derive(root x, [x], Modify)`; `store(a, r)`;
`b := derive(a, [x], Observe)`; `endUse(r)` is accepted and leaves `b` active with inactive origin
`a`. §51 "linked to a valid origin": holds if valid = exists (our `I2`), fails if valid = active.
The `free` analogue (owned `q` instead of `r`) behaves the same.

**SP-A4 §75 StaticPinnedBottom domain.** "Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places directly
owned by the base frame". Reading: only static indices (`l < statics.length`). Alternative (draft): every
`K.Pinned` leaf must be static and directly frame-0 owned. Example: `K.Pinned` on a local of frame 1:
our condition holds, draft's fails. Consequence: §73.3 rejects every exit of that frame.

**SP-A5 undefined clauses omitted** (no checkable content in `S3`): §60.1 "its origin chain and anchors
are valid" [policy]; §60.4 "footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true" [policy]; §62.5
[policy]; §63.6 "non-escape constraints" (undefined in v0; draft `NoEscape` removed); §64.2 "real
dependency" [policy]; §66.3 / §67.3 "type and storage contract", "constraints of the relevant types,
storage, and abstractions"; §72.2 "Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit
this change of holder"; §73.2 "Results that must survive have already been legally transferred";
§74 "respects applicable pinning obligations".

## B. Readings by clause

| # | Clause | Quote | Reading used | Alternative | Verdict change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | §43 | "over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable" / `HasRight` "over every leaf" | one authority for all leaves (∃∀) [policy] | ∀∃ | `split(root S,[[f1],[f2]])` then `pin(S)`: reject (∃∀) vs ok (∀∃) |

| 6 | §51 | "linked to a valid origin" | origin exists (draft) | origin active | W2 resulting state: I2 holds vs fails |
| 7 | §51 | "does not elevate its mode" | unconditional mode check [policy] | under ∀ p ∈ footprint (draft) | empty-footprint `Modify` derivative of an `Observe` origin: I2 fails vs holds |
| 8 | §53 | "A `Moved` leaf cannot be read" | `I4`: no `Read3Pre` of a region containing a `Moved` leaf (true by `Read3Pre.init`) | per-leaf `CanReadLeaf` (draft) | none |
| 9 | §47 | statics well-formedness | `StaticsOK` hypothesis of init theorems, not in `Reachable` [policy] | — | spec gap: cyclic statics break §57 at the initial state |

| 14 | §61.4 | "Creation ... respects origins, conservation I1/I2" | not a precondition [policy] | precondition | `split` under an unsound `DeclaredDisjoint` |

- `RootLive`: this is now `WF3.rootHeld` (plus the mode).
- `transfer_rootHeld`: it preserves the converse (`RootHeldConv`) under transfer. That is a

- All `*_preserves` proofs, `split_aux`, the RootLive preservation section
  (`exists_getElem?_of_mem` …) and the `Inv3.*` projections are out of scope.

## Could not be proved

None.

   ownership chains that are well-founded and reach a live frame (§49.3). `S3.Usable.frameOf`
   proves this in every state, without WF3, because `Usable` is inductive. The field therefore
   adds nothing beyond the inductive reading of §40.
2. **NoOrphan follows from WF3 alone** (`noOrphan_of_wf3`, using §49.2, §49.7 and §49.8). Under

3. **Suggested lemma, not added because it is outside the brief.** `ExercisableAt a m → ∃ y,
   s.A[a]? = some y ∧ y.active ∧ m.le y.mode` would discharge `hm` for derive and split.

- **Usability (§40)**: S3.Usable.mono/congr/of_eqs/of_same, HolderLive.congr, usable_of_partOf,
  usable_of_part.
- **Roots (§40, §49.6, §49.7)**:
  - rootOf_unique, exists_rootPlace, footprint_sub, exists_lt_not_of_not_forall,
    exists_mem_footprint (now on `hw.parent_lt`), RootChain.transport.
  - `RootHeldConv.transport` is the draft's `RootHeld.transport` under its new predicate name.
  - **New `RootHeld.transport`** for §49.7. It takes the same places, no new usable place, and
    active root authorities kept unchanged.
- **Additions and WF3 (§49–§53)**: addAuth_P/F/dead, rootChain_addAuth, addAuth_I1,
  addAuth_preserves. For addAuth_preserves:
  - **Adapted:** it has a new hypothesis `hm : m.le x.mode`, because I2 (§51) checks the mode
    unconditionally. In the draft, the mode check sat under `∀ p ∈ footprint`, so it was vacuous
    for an empty footprint.
  - Derive and split can discharge `hm` from `ExercisableAt src m`, since both constructors
    carry `m.le y.mode`.
  - The proof also covers the new WF3 content: §49.3 usable chains (via FrameOf.congr), §49.4
    leafhood, and §49.7 (via RootHeld.transport).
- **Transfer shape (§63)**: transfer_P_get, transfer_A_get, transfer_len, transfer_parentOf,
  transfer_footprint, transfer_partOf, mem_kids, kids_nil_iff, corrF_fuel, corr_src, corr_step,
  getElem?_mem, corr_partOf, mvTo_part, mvTo_place, transfer_owner_part, transfer_usable_part,
  transfer_pframe_part, transfer_skel, transfer_usable_back, transfer_usable_fwd. None of these
  read `D`, so the new `D` effect does not affect them.
- **NoOrphan (§54)**: mem_of_mem_dropWhile, linked_cons, linked_dropWhile, getLast?_cons_ne,
  getLast?_append_single, getLast?_dropWhile, length_dropWhile_le, dropWhile_ne_of_mem,
  dropLoops (def), mem_dropLoops, dropLoops_head, dropLoops_ne_nil, dropLoops_getLast,
  dropLoops_nodup, dropLoops_linked, linked_append, coversHolder_of, chain_to_frame.
  - `rootLive_cover` is now **rootHeld_cover**. It reads `hw.rootHeld` and ignores the mode.
  - **noOrphan_of_wf3 : WF3 s → NoOrphan s** replaces `noOrphan_of_rootLive`; there is no
    separate RootLive hypothesis any more.

## Dropped, and why

- `RootsDisjoint`, `rootsDisjoint_always`: the kernel has no `RootsDisjoint`, and WF3 has no such
  field. Its content survives as `rootOf_unique`.
- `pairwise_lt_range`: the brief forbids it (Classical.choice). In the draft only the `split`
  preservation proofs use it, so the split agent needs a choice-free replacement.
- `shared_keeps_exclusivity`: it restates I1 verbatim (§50) and is not a shared lemma.
- `write3_exclusive`: it is specific to one operation. `Write3Pre.exclusive` (§67.2) now gives
  it directly.
- The positional projections (WF3.origin/fp/ne/nodup/frames/ownerFrame/ownerPlace/parts/poss/
  rootChain/rootHeld) are replaced by the structure fields: `origins`, `footprints`,
  `frames.1/.2.1/.2.2`, `owners.1/.2.1`, `places`, `holders`, `rootChain`, `rootHeld`.
- `RootLive`: this is now `WF3.rootHeld` (plus the mode).
- `transfer_rootHeld`: it preserves the converse (`RootHeldConv`) under transfer. That is a
  preservation proof, left to the transfer agent; the draft proof should port verbatim.
- All `*_preserves` proofs, `split_aux`, the RootLive preservation section
  (`exists_getElem?_of_mem` …) and the `Inv3.*` projections are out of scope.

## Could not be proved

None.

## Observations for arbitration (no lemma blocked)

1. **The third conjunct of WF3.owners holds in every state.** For every usable place, it requires
   ownership chains that are well-founded and reach a live frame (§49.3). `S3.Usable.frameOf`
   proves this in every state, without WF3, because `Usable` is inductive. The field therefore
   adds nothing beyond the inductive reading of §40.
2. **NoOrphan follows from WF3 alone** (`noOrphan_of_wf3`, using §49.2, §49.7 and §49.8). Under
   these definitions, the `NoOrphan` conjunct of §57 is redundant given `WF3`. The argument
   matches §54 and does not rely on a permissive definition.
3. **Suggested lemma, not added because it is outside the brief.** `ExercisableAt a m → ∃ y,
   s.A[a]? = some y ∧ y.active ∧ m.le y.mode` would discharge `hm` for derive and split.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Lemmas

/-!
# Access kernel: the preserved invariant

The conjunction that every kernel step must preserve (§57) and the auxiliary invariant carried
with it. The per-operation preservation modules state their results with these two predicates.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The kernel invariant of §57: `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`. -/
def KInv (s : S3) : Prop := WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s

/-- Auxiliary invariant carried with `KInv` (§40, §49.7): the converse root-holder property
`RootHeldConv`, which is not a clause of `WF3`. -/
def KAux (s : S3) : Prop := RootHeldConv s

/-- `NoOrphan` follows from `WF3` (§54, §49.7), so `KInv` reduces to its first three
conjuncts. -/
theorem kInv_of {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hi : Inv3 s) (ha : AnchorOrderHeld s) : KInv s :=
  ⟨hw, hi, ha, noOrphan_of_wf3 hw⟩

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

{

  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation

The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.

## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. **All leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.

Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.

# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities

Frames are execution units that receive authorities, introduce locals, and have exit rules distinct from Spec 3's value-passing conventions.
## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline

A contract `K` parameterizes rules of the access discipline without fabricating permissions. A safe abstraction using part of `K` must prove or fulfill the corresponding obligation; an unestablished precondition is not a language guarantee.

| Contract | External obligation |
|---|---|
| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)`: no falsely declared disjoint region when leaves can overlap |
| `Pinned` | I5, prohibition of incompatible physical moves; `StaticPinnedBottom` for pinned statics |
| `SharedMutable` | Applicable shared-mutation discipline, with correct rights and synchronization |
| `ExternalDone` | External use of storage has ended when `unpin` is permitted |
| `Deallocable` | The place belongs to a unit that can actually be freed |
| `FreeCompat` | Opaque deallocation authority is compatible with the unit being freed |
| `Satisfiable` | The provider can satisfy the requested shape **in the current state** |

Structural conditions of `free`, dependencies, and the derived library `reset` carry the relevant invalidation obligations. Physical justification of `DDSound` must be established by a realization consistent with memory layouts and Section 82.

## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified

This specification **does not by itself determine**: concurrency and synchronization effects (Spec 2); control-flow analysis, `defer`, and by-value calling conventions (Spec 3); representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); representation of library metadata, address width, encodings, and alignment/ABI obligations (Spec 11); or final translation of `noalias` properties (Spec 13). Leaving a rule open does not authorize a safe interface to cause UB; the implementation must fulfill or reject the obligations before exposing the operation to safe code.

/-!
# Access kernel: state and derived notions

Abstract authority machine of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, Parts IV–VII:
frames (§39), places, leaves and footprints (§40), initialization states (§41), authorities
(§42), the state `S3` (§38), the external contract `K` (§48, §80), and the derived notions that
the operations of §60–§75 read: usability (§40), effective modes and exercisability (§43),
effective anchors and anchor order (§44), outcomes (§58).

Identities of places and authorities are list indices; index order represents acyclicity of
parent and origin links (§49, last paragraph). Reading decisions are recorded in the reference
pass readings, never in this file.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Frames (§39) -/

/-- Frame stack `F` (§39): frame identities, current frame first; the parent of a frame is the
next element. -/
abbrev Frames := List Nat

/-- `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` (§39): `f₁` is `f₂` or one of its ancestors in the stack. -/
def ancestor (F : Frames) (f₁ f₂ : Nat) : Prop := f₁ ∈ F.dropWhile (· != f₂)

/-- Decidability of `ancestor` (§39). -/
instance (F : Frames) (f₁ f₂ : Nat) : Decidable (ancestor F f₁ f₂) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∈ _))

/-! ## Parent chains (§40, §42) -/

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along the link `org`, nearest first, within fuel `k` (§40 structural
parents, §42 origins). Only links to a smaller index are followed (§49, last paragraph). -/
def chainF (org : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | 0, _ => []
  | k + 1, i =>
    match org i with
    | some o => if o < i then o :: chainF org k o else []
    | none => []

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along `org` (§40, §42); fuel `i` suffices since the chain
decreases. -/
def chain (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chainF org i i

/-! ## Places, leaves, footprints (§40) -/

/-- Holder of an authority (§42) or owner of a place (§40): a frame or a place. -/
inductive Holder where
  | frame (f : Nat)
  | place (p : Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Logical place (§40): optional structural parent, owner, abstract `kind`. Its identity is its
index in `P`; its death marker is `S3.dead`. -/
structure Place where
  parent : Option Nat
  owner : Holder
  kind : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Structural parent of place `i` (§40). -/
def parentOf (P : List Place) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (P[i]?).bind (·.parent)

/-- `partOf(p, q)` (§40): `p` is a place of `P` and `q` is `p` or one of its structural
ancestors. -/
def partOf (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop :=
  p < P.length ∧ (p = q ∨ q ∈ chain (parentOf P) p)

/-- Decidability of `partOf` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (partOf P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Leaf (§40): a place with no structural child. -/
def isLeaf (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Prop := ∀ r < P.length, parentOf P r ≠ some l

/-- Decidability of `isLeaf` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Decidable (isLeaf P l) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _, _))

/-- `footprint(q)` (§40): the leaves of `P` that are parts of `q`. -/
def footprint (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun l => decide (isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q)

/-- Two places overlap when their footprints share a leaf (§63.3). -/
def overlap (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := ∃ l ∈ footprint P p, l ∈ footprint P q

/-- Decidability of `overlap` (§63.3). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (overlap P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∃ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- `OwnedIn P src q` (§40, §33): the ownership chain of `q` reaches a place owned by `src` or by
one of its parts, that is, `q` is storage owned, directly or transitively, by the value at
`src`. -/
inductive OwnedIn (P : List Place) (src : Nat) : Nat → Prop where
  | direct {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → partOf P o src →
      OwnedIn P src q
  | step {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → OwnedIn P src o →
      OwnedIn P src q

/-! ## State (§38, §41, §42) -/

/-- Initialization state of a leaf (§41). -/
inductive InitSt where
  | uninit
  | init
  | moved
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Mode of an authority or of a request (§42, §43). -/
inductive Mode where
  | observe
  | modify
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Order of requested modes, `Observe ≤ Modify` (§43). -/
def Mode.le (m m' : Mode) : Prop := m = .observe ∨ m' = .modify

/-- Decidability of the mode order (§43). -/
instance (m m' : Mode) : Decidable (m.le m') := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∨ _))

/-- Authority (§42): own mode, optional origin, footprint (a list of leaves read
extensionally), holder, activity. Its identity is its index in `A`. -/
structure Authority where
  mode : Mode
  origin : Option Nat
  footprint : List Nat
  holder : Holder
  active : Bool
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- State `S3` (§38). `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D` are the components of §38. `nF` (next fresh frame
identity, §39), `dead` (death marker of places, §40) and `pin` (dynamic pinning of leaves, §74)
are auxiliary information that creates no right (§38). -/
structure S3 where
  F : Frames
  nF : Nat
  P : List Place
  I : Nat → InitSt
  A : List Authority
  D : Nat → List Nat
  dead : Nat → Bool
  pin : Nat → Bool

/-- Shape of the locals of `enterFrame` (§72) and of an allocation (§71.1): each element is an
optional structural parent (a place index) and a `kind`. Every element is owned by the holder
receiving the shape. -/
abbrev LocalShape := List (Option Nat × Nat)

/-- External contract `K` (§48, §80): `DeclaredDisjoint` on regions (§23, §61.3);
`SharedMutable` and `Pinned` on leaves (§68.1, §63.5); `ExternalDone` and `Deallocable` on places
(§75, §70.2); `FreeCompat place auth` (§70.2); `Satisfiable provider shape s` (§71). Obligations of
`K` are hypotheses of theorems, never fields. -/
structure K where
  DeclaredDisjoint : List Nat → List Nat → Prop
  SharedMutable : Nat → Prop
  Pinned : Nat → Prop
  ExternalDone : Nat → Prop
  Deallocable : Nat → Prop
  FreeCompat : Nat → Nat → Prop
  Satisfiable : Nat → LocalShape → S3 → Prop

/-- `DDSound(K)` (§80, §23): no declared disjointness relates two regions sharing a leaf. -/
def DDSound (k : K) : Prop := ∀ r r', k.DeclaredDisjoint r r' → ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r'

/-- `origin` link of authority `i` (§42). -/
def S3.org (s : S3) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (s.A[i]?).bind (·.origin)

/-- Strict ancestors of authority `i` along its origin chain (§42, §43). -/
def S3.ancs (s : S3) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chain s.org i

/-- Effective anchor of `x` (§44): the root reached along its origin chain, the last element of
`x :: s.ancs x`. -/
def S3.effAnchor (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Nat := (s.ancs x).getLastD x

/-- Active authority (§42); as an anchor, a valid anchor (§44). -/
def S3.Active (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Prop := ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y ∧ y.active = true

/-- Decidability of `S3.Active` (§42, §44). -/
instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Decidable (s.Active x) :=
  match h : s.A[x]? with
  | some y => if hy : y.active = true then isTrue ⟨y, h, hy⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨y', h', hy'⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact hy hy'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨_, h', _⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'

/-- Current frame, the top of the stack (§39). -/
def S3.top (s : S3) : Nat := s.F.headD 0

/-! ## Decidable helpers -/

/-- Predicate on an optional value, `P y` for `some y` and `d` for `none`; used to read the
components of `S3` (§38). -/
def OptP {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) : Prop :=
  match o with
  | some y => P y
  | none => d

/-- Decidability of `OptP` (§38). -/
instance {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) [DecidablePred P] [Decidable d] :
    Decidable (OptP o P d) :=
  match o with

rwa [kiter_ge h j] at hk

/-! ## Usable places (§40) -/

/-- `Usable(s, p)` (§40, items 1–3): `p` exists, is not marked dead, and its owner is a frame of
the stack or a usable place. Inductive, so an ownership cycle makes no place usable (§40). -/
inductive S3.Usable (s : S3) : Nat → Prop where
  | frame {q f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → s.dead q = false →
      pl.owner = .frame f → f ∈ s.F → S3.Usable s q
  | place {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → s.dead q = false →
      pl.owner = .place o → S3.Usable s o → S3.Usable s q

/-- A usable place exists (§40, item 1). -/
theorem S3.Usable.lt {s : S3} {q : Nat} (h : s.Usable q) : q < s.P.length := by
  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

/-- One step of `Usable` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
def usableR (s : S3) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
  match s.P[q]? with
  | some pl => !s.dead q && match pl.owner with
    | .frame f => decide (f ∈ s.F)
    | .place o => decide (o < s.P.length) && U o
  | none => false

/-- The place case of `usableR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
theorem usableR_place {s : S3} {U : Nat → Bool} {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} (hpl : s.P[q]? = some pl)
    (hd : s.dead q = false) (ho : pl.owner = .place o) (hlt : o < s.P.length) (hU : U o = true) :
    usableR s U q = true := by
  simp [usableR, hpl, hd, ho, hlt, hU]

/-- `usableR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §40). -/
theorem usableR_rule (s : S3) : KRule s.P.length (usableR s) where
  mono p q hpq a h := by
    unfold usableR at h ⊢; split at h
    · split at h <;> simp_all
    · exact h
  bound p a h := by
    unfold usableR at h; split at h
    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
    · cases h
  loc p q hpq a := by
    unfold usableR; split
    · split
      · rfl
      · rename_i o _; by_cases ho : o < s.P.length <;> simp [ho, hpq o]
    · rfl

/-- Soundness of the iteration for `Usable` (decision procedure for §40). -/
theorem usable_of_kiter (s : S3) : ∀ k q, kiter (usableR s) k q = true → s.Usable q
  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
  | k + 1, q, h => by
    simp only [kiter, usableR] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i pl hpl
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true'] at h
      obtain ⟨hd, h⟩ := h
      split at h
      · exact .frame hpl hd ‹_› (by simpa using h)
      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact .place hpl hd ‹_› (usable_of_kiter s k _ h.2)
    · cases h

/-- `Usable` is computed by `|P| + 1` steps of `usableR` (decision procedure for §40). -/
theorem usable_iff {s : S3} {q : Nat} :
    s.Usable q ↔ kiter (usableR s) (s.P.length + 1) q = true := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, usable_of_kiter s _ q⟩
  induction h with
  | frame hpl hd ho hf =>
    show usableR s _ _ = true
    simp [usableR, hpl, hd, ho, hf]
  | place hpl hd ho hu ih =>
    rw [← kiter_fix (usableR_rule s)]
    show usableR s _ _ = true
    exact usableR_place hpl hd ho hu.lt ih

/-- Decidability of `Usable` (§40). -/
instance (s : S3) (q : Nat) : Decidable (s.Usable q) := decidable_of_iff _ usable_iff.symm

/-- Live holder (§49.8): a frame of the stack or a usable place. -/
def HolderLive (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .frame f => f ∈ s.F
  | .place p => s.Usable p

/-- Decidability of `HolderLive` (§49.8). -/
instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderLive s h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold HolderLive <;> infer_instance

/-! ## Frame of a place (§40, §44) -/

/-- Frame ending the ownership chain of `q`, searched within `k` steps (`placeFrame`, §40). -/
def pframeF (s : S3) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
  | 0, _ => none
  | k + 1, q =>
    match s.P[q]? with
    | some pl =>
      match pl.owner with
      | .frame f => some f
      | .place o => pframeF s k o
    | none => none

/-- `placeFrame(q)` (§40): the frame ending the ownership chain of `q`, within `|P| + 1`
steps. -/
def S3.pframe (s : S3) (q : Nat) : Option Nat := pframeF s (s.P.length + 1) q

/-- Frame of a holder (§44): the frame itself, or the frame of the holding place. -/
def S3.hframe (s : S3) : Holder → Option Nat
  | .frame f => some f
  | .place p => s.pframe p

/-- `FrameOf s q f` (§40, `placeFrame`; §49.3): the ownership chain of `q` is finite and ends at
frame `f`. -/
inductive FrameOf (s : S3) : Nat → Nat → Prop where
  | frame {q f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → FrameOf s q f
  | place {q o f : Nat} {pl : Place} : s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → FrameOf s o f →
      FrameOf s q f

/-- A place with a frame exists (§40). -/
theorem FrameOf.lt {s : S3} {q f : Nat} (h : FrameOf s q f) : q < s.P.length := by
  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

/-- One step of `FrameOf s · f` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
    simp [frR, hpl, ho, ih, hf.lt]

/-! ## Transitive ownership (§40) -/

/-- One step of `OwnedIn P src` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §40). -/
def owR (P : List Place) (src : Nat) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
  match P[q]? with
  | some pl => match pl.owner with
    | .place o => decide (partOf P o src) || (decide (o < P.length) && U o)
    | .frame _ => false
  | none => false

/-- A place owned through the value at `src` exists (§40). -/
theorem OwnedIn.lt {P : List Place} {src q : Nat} (h : OwnedIn P src q) : q < P.length := by
  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›


/-! ## Effective modes (§43) -/

/-- Modes of the active descendants of `a` whose footprint covers leaf `p` (§43). -/
def descModes (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : List Mode :=
  (List.range s.A.length).filterMap fun j =>
    match s.A[j]? with
    | some y => if y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧ a ∈ s.ancs j then some y.mode else none
    | none => none

/-- Cases 2–4 of §43 for an active authority of own mode `m` covering the leaf, whose covering
active descendants have modes `ds`. -/
def effOf (m : Mode) (ds : List Mode) : Option Mode :=
  if ds = [] then some m else if Mode.modify ∈ ds then none else some .observe

/-- `effective(s, a, l)` (§43, cases 1–4), computed per leaf. -/
def effective (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Option Mode :=
  match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => if x.active = true ∧ p ∈ x.footprint then effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) else none
  | none => none

/-- Compatible effective modes for independent ordinary accesses: only `Observe`/`Observe`
(§50). -/
def Compat (m₁ m₂ : Mode) : Prop := m₁ = .observe ∧ m₂ = .observe

/-- Effective mode `e` permits the requested mode `m`: present and not exceeded (§43). -/
def Allows (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Prop := OptP e (fun e => m.le e) False

/-- Decidability of `Allows` (§43). -/
instance (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Allows e m) := by
  unfold Allows; infer_instance

/-- Footprint of authority `a` (§42), empty if it does not exist. -/
def S3.afp (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Nat := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => x.footprint
  | none => []

/-- Adds an authority with fresh identity `s.A.length` (§42, §60). -/
def S3.addAuth (s : S3) (y : Authority) : S3 := { s with A := s.A ++ [y] }

/-! ## Exercisable authorities (§43) -/

/-- `ExercisableAt(s, a, m)` (§43): `a` is active, its own mode permits `m`, and it is held by
the current frame, or by a place `p` such that an authority itself exercisable at `m` has an
effective mode permitting `m` on every leaf of `p`. Inductive along the holder chain (§43), so no
holder cycle justifies a right. -/
inductive S3.ExercisableAt (s : S3) : Nat → Mode → Prop where
  | base {a : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → m.le y.mode →
      y.holder = .frame s.top → S3.ExercisableAt s a m
  | held {a p b : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
      m.le y.mode → y.holder = .place p → S3.ExercisableAt s b m →
      (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) → S3.ExercisableAt s a m

/-- One step of `ExercisableAt · m` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure for §43). -/
def exR (s : S3) (m : Mode) (E : Nat → Bool) (a : Nat) : Bool :=
  match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => y.active && decide (m.le y.mode) && match y.holder with
    | .frame f => decide (f = s.top)
    | .place p => (List.range s.A.length).any fun b =>
        decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m) && E b
  | none => false

/-- `any` depends only on the values of the predicate on the list (decision procedure for
§43). -/
theorem any_congr' {α : Type} {f g : α → Bool} : ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ b ∈ l, f b = g b) →
    l.any f = l.any g
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    simp only [List.any_cons, h a (List.mem_cons_self ..),
      any_congr' fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb)]

/-- `exR` is a bounded monotone rule (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exR_rule (s : S3) (m : Mode) : KRule s.A.length (exR s m) where
  mono p q hpq a h := by
    unfold exR at h ⊢; split at h
    · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
      refine ⟨h.1, ?_⟩; split at h
      · simpa using h.2
      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, List.any_eq_true] at h ⊢
        obtain ⟨b, hb, hc, he⟩ := h.2
        exact ⟨b, hb, hc, hpq b he⟩
    · exact h
  bound p a h := by
    unfold exR at h; split at h
    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
    · cases h
  loc p q hpq a := by
    unfold exR; split
    · congr 1; split
      · rfl
      · exact any_congr' fun b hb => by rw [hpq b (List.mem_range.1 hb)]
    · rfl

/-- Soundness of the iteration for `ExercisableAt` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exercisableAt_of_kiter (s : S3) (m : Mode) :
    ∀ k a, kiter (exR s m) k a = true → s.ExercisableAt a m
  | 0, _, h => by simp [kiter] at h
  | k + 1, a, h => by
    simp only [kiter, exR] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i y hy
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨ha, hm⟩, h⟩ := h
      split at h
      · rename_i f hf; exact .base hy ha hm (by simp at h; rw [hf, h])
      · rename_i p hp
        simp only [List.any_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
        obtain ⟨b, -, hc, hb⟩ := h
        exact .held hy ha hm hp (exercisableAt_of_kiter s m k b hb) hc
    · cases h

/-- The frame-held case of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exR_base {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode)
    (hf : y.holder = .frame s.top) : exR s m E a = true := by
  unfold exR; rw [hy]; simp [ha, hm, hf]

/-- The place-held case of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exR_held {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a p b : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p)
    (hb : b < s.A.length) (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m)
    (hE : E b = true) : exR s m E a = true := by
  simp only [exR, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  exact ⟨hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩

/-- `ExercisableAt` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exercisableAt_iff {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    s.ExercisableAt a m ↔ kiter (exR s m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exercisableAt_of_kiter s m _ a⟩
  induction h with
  | base hy ha hm hf => exact exR_base hy ha hm hf
  | held hy ha hm hp hb hc ih =>
    rw [← kiter_fix (exR_rule s _)]
    have hb' := kiter_bound (exR_rule s _) _ _ ih
    exact exR_held hy ha hm hp hb' hc ih

/-- Decidability of `ExercisableAt` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (s.ExercisableAt a m) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ exercisableAt_iff.symm

/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43): the current frame has an authority exercisable at `m` whose
effective mode permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def HasRight (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.ExercisableAt a m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s a l) m

/-- Decidability of `HasRight` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Decidable (HasRight s m q) := by
  unfold HasRight; infer_instance

/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/

/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
are accounted for transitively). -/
def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D

/-- The anchors of every place containing leaf `p` are valid, that is, active (§44; §66.3,
§67.3, §68.3). -/
def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- Decidability of `DepsValid` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- The frame of the effective anchor of `x` (the frame of its holder) exists and is `fd` or an
ancestor of `fd` (§44). -/
def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False

/-- Decidability of `EffAnchorOK` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance

/-- `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54): for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, the frame of the
effective anchor of `x` is the frame of `q` or an ancestor. -/
def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P` (decision procedure for §44). -/
theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩

/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrder` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrder s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrder_iff.symm

/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): the rule of `AnchorOrder` for every active authority held by a
usable place `q`. -/
def AnchorOrderHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
    y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` read on the places of `P` and the authorities of `A` (decision procedure for
§44). -/
theorem anchorOrderHeld_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrderHeld s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
        EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)) True := by
  constructor
  · intro h q _ hq x _
    unfold OptP; split
    · rename_i y hy; exact h q hq x y hy
    · trivial
  · intro h q hq x y hy ya hh
    have := h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
    simp only [OptP, hy] at this; exact this ya hh

/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrderHeld s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrderHeld_iff.symm

/-! ## Outcomes (§58) -/

/-- `Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail` (§58). `fail` leaves the state unchanged and
carries none. -/
inductive Outcome3 (σ : Type) where
  | ok (s : σ)
  | reject
  | fail

/-- A kernel transition other than `alloc` (§58): `ok` with the effect when the preconditions
hold, `reject` otherwise; never `fail`. -/
inductive Guarded {σ : Type} (Pre : Prop) (eff : σ) : Outcome3 σ → Prop where
  | ok : Pre → Guarded Pre eff (.ok eff)
  | reject : ¬ Pre → Guarded Pre eff .reject

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Basic

/-!
# Access kernel: operations O1–O16

The sixteen kernel operations of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` §60–§75. Each
operation has a precondition structure with one named field per clause item (or per condition of
an item), each field citing its clause; a `Decidable` instance; an effect function; and a step
relation over `Outcome3` (§58). Every operation except `alloc` is `Guarded` (`ok` or `reject`);
`alloc` may also `fail` (§58, §71). `KStep` is the union of their `ok` transitions.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- `mapI f i l` applies `f` to each element of `l` with its index counted from `i` (used by the
effects of §72 and §73). -/
def mapI {α β : Type} (f : Nat → α → β) : Nat → List α → List β
  | _, [] => []
  | i, a :: l => f i a :: mapI f (i + 1) l

/-! ## O1 `derive` (§60) -/

/-- Effect of `derive(source, region, mode)` (§60, `ok` effect): a new active authority of fresh
identity, origin `src`, mode `m`, footprint `region`, held by the current frame. -/
def deriveEff (s : S3) (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  s.addAuth ⟨m, some src, region, .frame s.top, true⟩

/-- Preconditions of `derive` (§60). -/

/-- `derive` as a relation (§60). -/
def DeriveStep (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) (m : Mode) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (DerivePre s src region m) (deriveEff s src region m)

/-! ## Shapes (§47, §71.1, §72) -/

/-- A local shape as a shape whose elements have no owning element (§71.1, §72: locals and
allocated storage are owned by the receiving holder). -/
def LocalShape.toShape (ls : LocalShape) : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) :=
  ls.map fun e => (e.1, none, e.2)

/-- Owner of element `i` of a shape (§47, §72, §71): its owning element if any, `hd`
otherwise. -/
def shapeOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  | none => hd

/-- Places `P` followed by the elements of a shape (§47, §71, §72): (parent, owning element,
kind), owned by their owning element or by `hd`. -/
def shapeP (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    List Place :=
  P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Well-formed shape at offset `n` (§72.2, §71.1; for statics, the hypothesis recorded for
§47): the parent and the owning element of an element are earlier elements, and a part has the
owning element of its parent. -/
def ShapeOK (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - n]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => n ≤ o ∧ o < n + i) True

/-- Decidability of `ShapeOK` (§72.2, §71.1). -/
instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

/-- Indices of the root elements (no parent) of a shape (§40 root places; §47, §71, §72). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (§72) -/

/-- Places after `enterFrame` (§72, `ok` effect): the locals appended, owned by the new frame. -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : LocalShape) : List Place := shapeP s.P (.frame s.nF) ls.toShape

/-- Effect of `enterFrame(params, locals)` (§72, `ok` effect): a new frame `nF` is pushed; the
parameters are now held by it; locals are appended (uninitialized, no anchor, alive, unpinned)
with one active root `Modify` authority per root local, held by the new frame. -/
def enterEff (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : S3 :=
  { F := s.nF :: s.F, nF := s.nF + 1, P := enterP s ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit else s.I l
    A := mapI (fun j y => if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s.nF } else y) 0 s.A ++
      (rootIdx ls.toShape).map fun i =>
        ⟨.modify, none, footprint (enterP s ls) (s.P.length + i),
          shapeOwner ls.toShape (.frame s.nF) i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
instance (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : Decidable (EnterPre s ps ls) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.F ≠ [] ∧ (∀ a ∈ ps, OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧
      y.holder = .frame s.top ∧ y.origin ≠ none) False) ∧ ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape ∧
    (∀ p ∈ ps, ParamOriginHidden (enterEff s ps ls) p) ∧ AnchorOrderHeld (enterEff s ps ls))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩⟩

def EnterStep (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EnterPre s ps ls) (enterEff s ps ls)

/-! ## O14 `alloc` (§71) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `alloc provider owner shape` (§71, items 1–3). -/
structure AllocStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : Prop where
  /-- §71.1: the shape is nonempty. -/
  nonempty : ls ≠ []
  /-- §71.1: the shape is represented like the locals of `enterFrame` (each parent is an earlier
  element). -/
  shapeOK : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape
  /-- §71.1 with the `ok` outcome of §71 ("a new storage root"): exactly one element has no
  parent. -/
  oneRoot : (rootIdx ls.toShape).length = 1
  /-- §71.2: all leaves of the provider are `Init`. -/
  providerInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P provider, s.I l = .init
  /-- §71.2: metadata updates are permitted through exercisable `Modify` on the provider or a
  valid `writeShared` (§68) over its leaves. -/
  providerRight : HasRight s .modify provider ∨
    ∃ via ∈ List.range s.A.length, WriteSharedPre k s via (footprint s.P provider)
  /-- §71.3: exercisable `Modify` over `owner`. -/
  ownerRight : HasRight s .modify owner
  /-- §71.3 (liveness restrictions): `owner` is usable. -/
  ownerUsable : s.Usable owner

/-- Decidability of the static preconditions of `alloc` (§71). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat)
    (ls : LocalShape) : Decidable (AllocStatic k s provider owner ls) :=
  decidable_of_iff (ls ≠ [] ∧ ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape ∧ (rootIdx ls.toShape).length = 1 ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P provider, s.I l = .init) ∧
    (HasRight s .modify provider ∨
      ∃ via ∈ List.range s.A.length, WriteSharedPre k s via (footprint s.P provider)) ∧
    HasRight s .modify owner ∧ s.Usable owner)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g⟩⟩

/-- Places after `alloc` (§71, `ok` outcome): the elements of the shape appended, owned by
`owner`. -/
def allocP (s : S3) (owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : List Place :=
  shapeP s.P (.place owner) ls.toShape

/-- Effect of `alloc` (§71, `ok` outcome): a new storage root of fresh identities owned by
`owner`, its leaves `Uninit`, no anchor, alive, unpinned, with a root `Modify` authority with no
origin held by `owner`. -/
def allocEff (s : S3) (owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := allocP s owner ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit else s.I l
    A := s.A ++ (rootIdx ls.toShape).map fun i =>
      ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s owner ls) (s.P.length + i),
        shapeOwner ls.toShape (.place owner) i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.dead q
    pin := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.pin q }

/-- `alloc provider owner shape` as a relation (§71 outcomes, §58): `reject` when a static
precondition fails; `fail`, state unchanged, when `K.Satisfiable` is false; `ok` otherwise. -/
inductive AllocStep (k : K) (provider owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (s : S3) :
    Outcome3 S3 → Prop where
  | ok : AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → k.Satisfiable provider ls s →
      AllocStep k provider owner ls s (.ok (allocEff s owner ls))
  | fail : AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → ¬ k.Satisfiable provider ls s →
      AllocStep k provider owner ls s .fail
  | reject : ¬ AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → AllocStep k provider owner ls s .reject

/-! ## O15 `pin`, O16 `unpin` (§74, §75) -/

/-- Preconditions of `pin` (§74). "Applicable pinning obligations" is not represented. -/
structure PinPre (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §74: `place` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §74: exercisable `Modify` over the leaves of `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `pin` (§74). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (PinPre s p) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `pin` (`b = true`, §74) and `unpin` (`b = false`, §75): the dynamic pinning flag of
the leaves of `place`. -/
def pinEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) (b : Bool) : S3 :=
  { s with pin := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then b else s.pin l }

/-- `pin` as a relation (§74). -/
def PinStep (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (PinPre s p) (pinEff s p true)

/-- Preconditions of `unpin` (§75). -/
structure UnpinPre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §75: `place` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §75: exercisable `Modify` over `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §75: `K.ExternalDone(place)`. -/
  externalDone : k.ExternalDone p

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `unpin` (§75). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] (s : S3) (p : Nat) :
    Decidable (UnpinPre k s p) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧ k.ExternalDone p)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩

/-- `unpin` as a relation (§75). -/
def UnpinStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (UnpinPre k s p) (pinEff s p false)

/-! ## Kernel steps (§57, §58) -/

/-- One `ok` transition of a kernel operation O1–O16 (§60–§75; §57 reachability). -/
inductive KStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | derive {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {region : List Nat} {m : Mode} :
      DeriveStep src region m s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | split {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {rs : List (List Nat)} :
      SplitStep k src rs s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | release {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | transfer {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | depend {s s' : S3} {q x : Nat} : DependStep q x s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | enter {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | exit {s s' : S3} : ExitStep k s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | read {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Read3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | write {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Write3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | writeShared {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} :
      WriteSharedStep k a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | pin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : PinStep p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | unpin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : UnpinStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | endUse {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : EndUseStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | free {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | alloc {s s' : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | store {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} : StoreStep a p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access
